records.issue_text: Hosts stored with ports can validate but never match requests because URI parsing omits the port while comparison uses the stored host including it.
records.rationale: The validation regex in EmbeddableHost allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), and the before_validation only strips the protocol and path but preserves the port in the host field. However, in record_for_host, URI(host).host returns just the hostname without the port. records.issue_text: Host mappings allow duplicates because neither a uniqueness validation nor database unique index exists; lookup then chooses an arbitrary category.
records.rationale: The diff shows the EmbeddableHost model in app/models/embeddable_host.rb with only a format validation on host, no uniqueness validation. The migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table without a unique index on the host column. The lookup method record_for_host uses .first which would return an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. This is a real defect - d

records.issue_text: Hostname validation restricts TLDs to 2–5 letters, rejecting valid modern TLDs and IDN/punycode domains.
records.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb a regex validation: validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i. This regex restricts TLDs to 2-5 letters ([a-z]{2,5}), which would reject valid modern TLDs like .museum (6 chars), .technology (10 chars), and many new gTLDs.
